entries.title: When a Canadian town provided safe haven on 9/11
entries.post_content:
When 7,000 Strangers Found Home in Gander

A small Canadian town's sudden influx of international travelers after 9/11.

For five days, a town's hospitality was put to the ultimate test.

In the aftermath of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, the small town of Gander in Newfoundland, Canada, was thrust into the spotlight as a refuge for thousands of stranded passengers and crew members from around the world. The town's population more than doubled, as 38 international flights were grounded on the island. For five days, residents came together to provide shelter, food, and comfort to the "plane people."

Newfoundlanders' generosity and kindness were on full display as they welcomed the strangers into their homes and hearts. The town's mayor at the time, Paul Bannerman, has said that the experience was a defining moment for the community, highlighting the importance of kindness and compassion in the face of crisis.

The selfless acts of the Gander residents have become a source of inspiration, leading to the creation of the Broadway musical "Come From Away." The show has told the story of the town's remarkable hospitality and the impact it had on the lives of the passengers and crew who were stranded there.

What do you think would have happened if this had happened in a more isolated or fragmented world? How would you have reacted in this situation? Let us know 👇
